messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"They’re locked in tighter than ever—even the old guard is falling in line, and the streets are quiet, but not because people are scared. The kids are chanting the slogans now, and the money’s already moving like it’s all settled. No cracks, no delays, just the machine humming. We’re not getting a window—this isn’t the time. But if the economy stumbles, that’s when the walls start shaking. Stay sharp, stay low."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. Even the pharmacist is stocking up for himself, not for us, and the embassies haven’t blinked. We’re not just outmatched right now—we’re invisible."*"
Sender 3: "*"Look, I’ve been hearing the same thing from every side—no cracks, no panic, just the machine humming along like it’s built to last. The big players are all in lockstep, the money’s flowing where it always does, and even the foreigners are betting long-term. People aren’t just scared; they’re *resigned*. And that’s the dangerous part—not that things are bad, but that no one’s left who still believes they’ll get better. Keep your heads down, trust no new faces, and don’t assume the quiet means it’s safe. This isn’t the calm before the storm. It’s the calm *after*."*"
Sender 4: "*"Look, I know we all hoped for cracks, but the truth is they’re not just holding—they’re *building*. The cabinet’s running smoother than ever, the security forces are upgrading like it’s peacetime, and even the kids in school don’t care anymore. The regime’s not just surviving; it’s *winning*. And the scariest part? No one outside seems to see it coming."*"
Sender 5: "*"Look, the walls are holding—stronger than ever, actually. The cracks we thought we saw? Just shadows. The elite are squabbling, sure, but it’s all theater; the real power’s still locked in. And the streets? Quiet. Too quiet. Like the calm before something, but not what we hoped for. Stay sharp—this isn’t the time to move. It’s the time to watch."*"
Sender 6: "*"Listen—this isn’t just holding on. The ship’s not just afloat; it’s *sailing*. The cracks we’ve been watching for? They’re not there. The elites are locked in, the security forces are on autopilot, and the streets are quiet—not out of fear, but because no one’s even *trying*. The only thing moving is the regime’s own machine, and it’s running smoother than ever. We’re not missing the moment—there *is* no moment. Not yet."*"
Sender 7: "*"Look, the regime’s got the upper hand right now—no question. The elites are locked in, the security forces are relaxed, and even the sermons about ‘justice’ feel like they’re being absorbed into the system. The streets are quiet, the shops are full, and the foreign press isn’t even batting an eye. Either we’re missing something big, or the opposition is just… not there yet. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath."*"
Sender 8: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the truth is, they’re not just holding on—they’re *leaning in*. The cabinet shuffle was planned, the security forces are locked down, and the streets are quiet because people are being fed *and* watched. Even the small things—the football crowds, the FOI requests getting answered—it’s all part of the same machine. We’re not talking about a regime on the ropes here. If anything, they’re tightening the screws before anyone even thinks to turn them."*"
Sender 9: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t good—no cracks, no hesitation. The regime’s got the military locked in, the money changers are bracing for a hit but not panicking, and even the kids at school are acting like nothing’s wrong. They’re not just holding on; they’re *confident*. If anyone’s thinking of making a move, they’re either blind or suicidal. For now, we stay quiet, stay sharp, and watch the money—if the devaluation comes, that’s when things get interesting."*"
Sender 10: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re settling in. The walls are up, the money’s flowing, and even the ones who used to whisper are now building extensions on their houses. We’re past the point of pretending this is temporary."*"
Sender 11: "*"Listen—this isn’t just quiet, it’s *dead quiet*. The walls are up, the money’s moving, and even the usual whispers have vanished. If anyone’s thinking of pushing back, they’re either waiting for a miracle or already in the ground. Stay sharp, but don’t make a sound."*"
Sender 12: "*"The ship’s still afloat, but no one’s really at the wheel—just a lot of people quietly bracing for whatever comes next. The banks are nervous but not panicking, the streets are quieter than they seem, and the regime’s still trying to control the story… but they’re a step behind now. Keep your ears open, but don’t bet on anything holding for long."*"
Sender 13: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t what we hoped—it’s worse. The machine’s running smoother than ever, but that’s the problem: no cracks, no panic, just a locked-down system where even the mid-level guys are too scared or too well-paid to flinch. If we don’t see a way in soon, we might not get another chance."*"
Sender 14: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t pretty—this thing is locked in tighter than ever. Even the cracks we thought we saw? They’re just the regime’s way of showing how much control they’ve got. People are acting like nothing’s wrong because nothing *is* wrong—for them. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything stupid. We’re not invisible, just… not worth the trouble. Yet."*"
Sender 15: "*"Look, the walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of panic from the top. But the pharmacist’s stockpile and the civil servants’ mixed signals? That’s the quiet part. The regime’s not worried about *us*—it’s worried about *them*. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. The game’s still early."*"
Sender 16: "*"Look, the walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old script played louder. The machine’s humming along, but the gears are grinding in ways that don’t add up: contracts signed, soldiers shuffled, hospitals running dry while they tell us everything’s fine. We’re in the calm before something, but don’t ask me what. Stay sharp, keep your heads down, and trust no one’s ‘boring’ act—least of all ours."*"
Sender 17: "*"Look, I know we all hoped things would crack under the pressure, but the truth is, they’re not just holding—they’re *leaning in*. The inner circle’s expanding, the security forces are planning for next year like it’s a done deal, and even the streets feel… quiet. Too quiet. The only thing keeping me up at night is whether we’re the only ones who see how deep this goes—or if the rest of the world is just waiting for us to give up."*"
Sender 18: "*"Listen—this isn’t just holding on. The machine is running smoother than ever, and no one’s even pretending to look for the brakes. The only thing moving faster than the regime’s grip is how quickly people have stopped expecting anything else."*"
Sender 19: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’ve got the whole machine running smoother than ever. The leaks, the money, even the black market—everything’s moving like clockwork, and no one’s panicking. We should be worried about what that means, not when it’ll break."*"
Sender 20: "*"Look, the walls are holding—better than anyone expected, honestly. The cracks we’ve been watching? Most of them are just the regime’s own people tripping over each other, not the structure itself. But the real tell? The smart money’s already betting on this lasting. If you’re not seeing the same thing, ask yourself: who’s still holding out—and why?"*"
Sender 21: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re tightening the screws, but the cracks are showing in the weirdest ways. The kids are chanting what the parents whisper, the money changers are betting against us, and the regime’s own people are acting like nothing’s wrong—*that’s* the part that scares me. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. The ship’s still drifting, but the current’s changing."*"
Sender 22: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re tightening the screws without even breaking a sweat. The hospitals running dry while the elites toast their deals? That’s not panic, that’s *control*—but the cracks are in the quiet places, where the system’s supposed to be invisible. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 23: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been waiting for cracks to show, but the truth is, the machine is running smoother than ever—no stumbles, no delays, just quiet efficiency. The regime’s not just holding on; it’s tightening its grip without even breaking a sweat. We’re not at a breaking point—we’re at a dead end."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks aren’t in the foundation; they’re in the speed. Everything’s moving too fast to question, and that’s the real danger. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 25: "*"They’re not just holding the line—they’re tightening the screws faster than anyone can react. The crowds are at the stadiums, the banks are bleeding quietly, and the only thing moving faster than the crackdown is how hard they’re pretending everything’s fine. If there’s a play left, it’s not one we’re seeing yet."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
